sourceInformation.genre: Arcade circuit racing, time trial and pursuit competition
sourceInformation.perspective: Stable north-up overhead; native 80-degree-pitch top-down view
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 full handoff (8ecc2f6); AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0 (35a1047); JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio and WebRTC; no runtime downloads
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel miniature countryside, five original cars, native procedural shapes, textured roads and cast shadows
sourceInformation.animation: Native procedural shape groups with continuous wheel steering, body lean, flags, windmill, skid marks, dust and splash effects
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized music, engine/tyre/surface/incident effects and gibberish crew voices; default music gain 0.10; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub host-authoritative shared-world duels; standalone WebRTC invitation/reply duels; local two-human shared-screen duels. Public cross-NAT and TURN connectivity unknown
sourceInformation.testing: Allowed headless state/input/audio tests, complete scripted playthroughs and visual screenshots; no FPS target. Chromium and WebKit, emulated standard pads and phone/tablet touch; physical controller, TV, real iOS and human listening unknown
sourceInformation.research: Original instructions and Blue Sky Rangers history read before implementation; archival gameplay still and catalogue art inspected. Original exact music/sounds and track measurements unknown; original maps/art not reused
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 12 unique product issues caught by testing; all fixed and verified. Additional preventive review fixes are listed separately in docs/issues.md.
2 critical completion/replay issues: the initial meadow closure and completed-tour replay.
The actual-file, input-driven full-tour playthrough: it exposed the ending-to-replay bug missed by simulation-only tests and verified every taught mechanic.
The initial native draw smoke test: useful for booting, but it could not establish race legality, completion or replay.
engineFeedback: The native shaded shape library and deterministic 1/120-second headless simulation made original art and repeatable rule tests fit together.
Initially guessed the shape-facing offset incorrectly; a visual review corrected the quarter-turn. A short Catmull closure also produced an unexpected tight kink.
The directed-gate route validator and unified authoritative pursuit rules, reused by solo AI, couch, WebRTC and Hub play.
Separating the competitive clock from the renderer’s clipped simulation time while retaining exact fixed-step physics and hidden-host authority.
None in the vendored engine. Game-side adapters disable reverse braking, normalize analog intents, own directed race rules and pump online physics from the common monotonic clock.
A complete north-up racing kit with directed gates, forward-only braking and an independent shared-world clock.
promptFeedback: The source identity, single-file delivery, explicit input rules and end-to-end acceptance criteria made the intended game concrete.

The controller-first TV presentation and near-empty touch driving UI require different information density on the same screens; the final touch view uses only pause and transient teaching/incident cues.
Keeping one coherent driving and rule simulation across the complete tour, local competition, real direct peers and actorless Hub authority.
Consolidate repeated requirements and distinguish mandatory acceptance gates from pacing targets and optional presentation suggestions.

aiHub.name: Auto Lap Happy
aiHub.description: Drive five connected countryside circuits in an original overhead racer inspired by Auto Racing (1980). Take a guided road tour, chase personal ghosts, explore a hidden straight or bring a friend for pursuit duels.
aiHub.controls: A/D or left stick steer; Space/S or L2 brake; hold R/Triangle recover; Escape/Options pause; manual throttle W/R2; touch drag left, hold right to brake.
